title: 1. THE REVERSED PROCESSOR
prompt: A processor receives the following 8-bit instruction. Apply the correct processor procedure and report the final 8-bit output.
summary: 8-bit word procedure: Full reversal -> Invert every bit -> Split into two 4-bit nibbles and exchange left/right nibbles.

title: 2. THE FORBIDDEN GATE
prompt: Evaluate the circuit from left to right. Report the single output bit.
code:
A = 1
B = 1
C = 1

A and B enter G1. The output of G1 and C enter G2.
summary: G1 outputs 1 when exactly one input is 1. G2 outputs 1 when its two inputs are different.

title: 3. THE MEMORY FRAGMENT
prompt: Execute the following instruction sequence using the memory table. Report the final 4-bit result.
code:
M1 = 1100
M2 = 1011
M3 = 0101
M4 = 0110

READ M2
XOR M4
AND M1
NOT RESULT
summary: Execute operations sequentially on 4-bit registers: READ M2, XOR M4, AND M1, NOT RESULT.

title: 4. THE CLOCK SYNCHRONIZATION ERROR
prompt: Four machines report different times. Use the synchronization procedure to determine the master time.
code:
Machine A = 14:20
Machine B = 14:08
Machine C = 14:32
Machine D = 14:26
summary: For 4 clock readings: sort them, discard earliest and latest, average the remaining two. Round down seconds.

title: 5. THE CORRUPTED TRANSMISSION
prompt:
A system receives the following 7-bit data.

Check whether the data is valid. If an error is detected, apply the correction procedure and report the corrected data.
code: RECEIVED = 1101011
summary: For 7-bit word, total 1s must be even. If odd, assume the final bit is corrupted and flip only that bit.

title: 6. THE ROUTER'S DILEMMA
prompt:
A packet must travel from Router A to Router F.

Find the lowest-cost route and report its total cost.
code:
Available routes:
A → B → D → F
A → C → E → F
A → B → E → F

Connection costs:
A-B = 5
B-D = 2
D-F = 3
A-C = 3
C-E = 2
E-F = 1
B-E = 4
summary: Add link costs. Tie-break: fewer links, then alphabetical next-hop.

title: 7. THE EXPIRING PACKET
prompt:
A packet begins with TTL = 10 and travels through the following devices:

Router A → Switch B → Router C → Router D → Destination

Determine whether the packet reaches its destination and calculate its remaining TTL.
code:
INITIAL TTL = 10
PATH: Router A → Switch B → Router C → Router D → Destination
summary: Every router decreases TTL by 2. Every switch decreases TTL by 1. Discard if TTL <= 0.

title: 8. THE FIREWALL CODE
prompt:
A security system receives the following six-bit authentication token.

Transform the token using the firewall procedure and report the final six-bit token.
code: TOKEN = 100110
summary: For 6-bit token: reverse the bits, XOR with 110011, then rotate left by 2 positions.

title: 9. THE LOST PASSWORD
prompt:
A message has been encrypted using a Caesar cipher.

Decrypt the message and report the original uppercase word.
code:
MODE = C3
ENCRYPTED = ZRUOG
summary: For C3: decrypt by shifting each letter 3 places backward in the alphabet (A wraps to Z).

title: 10. THE AUTHENTICATION SEQUENCE
prompt:
A security system requires a six-digit authentication code.

The following values are provided:

A = 5
B = 8
C = 3
D = 2
E = 4
F = 1

Generate the valid six-digit authentication code.
summary: Digits in exact order: (A+C) last digit; |B-D|; (E*F) last digit; A+F; C+E; B-F.

title: 11. THE LOOP THAT NEVER ENDS
prompt: Execute the following pseudocode exactly and report the values printed.
code:
x = 3
count = 0

while x < 40:
    x = x * 2
    count = count + 1

print(x, count)
summary: Execute the while loop strictly from top to bottom. Report printed x and count.

title: 12. THE STACK OVERFLOW MYSTERY
prompt:
A stack receives the following operations:

Determine the final stack contents from bottom to top.
code:
PUSH 15
PUSH 25
POP
PUSH 35
PUSH 45
POP
PUSH 55
PUSH 65
POP
summary: LIFO stack: PUSH adds to top, POP removes from top. Report bottom to top.

title: 13. THE DEADLOCK SEQUENCE
prompt:
Three processes are requesting resources.

P1 holds R1 and needs R3.
P2 holds R2 and needs R1.
P3 holds R3 and needs R2.

No resources are initially available.

Determine whether the system is deadlocked.
If a deadlock exists, apply the recovery procedure and report the completion order of the remaining processes.
code:
P1 holds R1 and needs R3.
P2 holds R2 and needs R1.
P3 holds R3 and needs R2.
No resources available.
summary: Terminate process with lowest number (P1). Released resources satisfy waiting processes.

title: 14. THE DATABASE DETECTIVE
prompt:
A database contains the following records:

Execute the following SQL query and report the resulting Name column in order.
code:
ID  | Name | Score
101 | A    | 82
102 | B    | 68
103 | C    | 91
104 | D    | 74
105 | E    | 88

SELECT Name
FROM Students
WHERE Score > 75
ORDER BY Score DESC;
summary: Filter Score > 75 strictly. Sort descending by score. Display Name column.

title: 15. THE CACHE REPLACEMENT MYSTERY
prompt:
A cache has three available slots.

The following memory requests arrive:

B, C, A, B, D, C, E

Using the cache replacement protocol, determine the final cache contents.
Report the contents from least recently used to most recently used.
code:
Requests: B, C, A, B, D, C, E
Slots: 3
Protocol: LRU
summary: On hit mark accessed as MRU. On miss when full, evict LRU. Report oldest to newest.

title: 16. THE AI CLASSIFICATION TRAP
prompt:
An AI model receives the following features:

Calculate the final score and determine the classification.
code:
Temperature = 22
Humidity = 35
Rainfall = 8
PROFILE = RISK-3

Score = (Temperature × 2) + (Humidity × 1) - (Rainfall × 3)
summary: RISK-3 bands: below 50 = LOW; 50 through 70 inclusive = MODERATE; above 70 = HIGH.

title: 17. THE NEAREST NEIGHBOUR
prompt:
An AI system must classify a new object:

X = (3,3)

Use the three nearest neighbours to determine the class of X.
code:
X = (3,3)

Training dataset:
A = (1,1), RED
B = (3,2), RED
C = (2,4), RED
D = (5,5), BLUE
E = (4,3), BLUE
summary: Calculate Euclidean distances. Select 3 smallest distances. Majority vote decides class.

title: 18. THE NEURAL NETWORK BLACK BOX
prompt:
A neural network receives two inputs:

Calculate the final output of the network.
code:
Inputs: X1 = 0, X2 = 1
Weights:
X1 → H1 = 3
X2 → H1 = 1
X1 → H2 = 2
X2 → H2 = 2
H1 → O = 1
H2 → O = 1
summary: Threshold: sum >= 2 gives 1; otherwise 0. Calculate hidden activations then output activation.

title: 19. THE ROBOT WITH A BROKEN COMPASS
prompt:
A robot begins at coordinate (0,0), facing North.

It receives the following commands:

F, F, R, F, F, F, R, F, L, F

Determine its final coordinates and direction.
code:
Start: (0,0), facing North
Commands: F, F, R, F, F, F, R, F, L, F
(North=+Y, East=+X, South=-Y, West=-X)
summary: F moves 1 unit in facing direction. R turns 90° clockwise. L turns 90° anticlockwise.

title: 20. THE ALGORITHM THAT LIES
prompt:
A machine receives the following array:

Execute the algorithm exactly as written and report the final array.
summary: Trace the nested loop swapping whenever A[i] < A[j]. Every swap takes effect immediately.
